name: Loop-Invariant Load Hoisting
matchText: Loop-Invariant Load Hoisting: A load or computation inside a loop has an address or operands that depend only on outer-loop values or kernel parameters, so every iteration (or every row program) reloads the same value and the load can be hoisted above the loop.
content:
Problem:
The same parameter or lookup value is repeatedly fetched as the loop advances, for example a
bias or RMS-weight vector whose address depends only on the column index r1 but is reloaded
inside every row iteration.

Recommended changes:
- Derive each load address symbolically and identify which loop variables it depends on.
- Move a load immediately outside the deepest loop whose induction variable it does not use.
- Preload the bias/RMS vectors before the persistent row loop so only the per-row data loads
  issue each iteration.

Constraints:
- Do not hoist loads across stores that may alias the same address.
- Ensure preloaded vectors fit in UB and preserve masks and default values.
